title: O2-transfer × assimilable-N carbon-allocation switch gate
question: Does a reproducible interaction between oxygen-transfer state and assimilable-nitrogen availability create a narrow regime in which cells remain metabolically active while a larger fraction of consumed carbon is recovered as extracellular bacterial cellulose?

o2_transfer_axis.rule: The factor is measured oxygen-transfer state, not nominal gas fraction.

primary_endpoint.name: BC_CARBON_ALLOCATION_PROXY
primary_endpoint.interpretation: Allocation proxy only unless carbon-balance closure criteria are met.

stage_b_selection_rule.rule: Identify the largest adjacent change in the preregistered allocation endpoint across the 3x3 grid, then place midpoint and flank confirmation points by a frozen deterministic rule; Stage-B data cannot redefine the rule.
stage_b_selection_rule.purpose: Densify a possible narrow transition without outcome-driven hand tuning.

decision_rules.if: additive model predicts held-out data as well as or better than interaction/switch models
dry BC mass changes but carbon-allocation proxy does not
candidate ridge coincides with loss of cell activity or severe biomass collapse
carbon balance is incomplete or outside closure acceptance
interaction improves held-out prediction and a noncollapsed ridge repeats independently
R4 plus an orthogonal rescue can move the mediator vector across and back over the ridge without changing N-source identity or source-factor availability

kill_rules: Reject switch language if CO2 systematically tracks O2-transfer levels outside frozen bounds.
Reject nitrogen-amount interpretation if nitrogen source identity changes across the primary surface.
Reject carbon-flux language if only BC dry mass is measured.
Reject allocation-switch interpretation if the apparent ridge is explained by cell death or gross growth collapse.
Reject a universal switch if the geometry fails independent-batch replication.
Reject O2-specific language if the effect is better explained by shear, bubble-size, or transfer-geometry changes not captured by measured transfer state.

literature_anchors.note: Nanobubble OTR was much higher than airlift, increased cell density, but BNC volumetric productivity remained similar to airlift; carbon allocation therefore cannot be inferred from oxygen supply alone.
2026 K. xylinus study normalizing total nitrogen showed strong nitrogen-dependent production differences and discussed metabolic balance.
Nitrogen source significantly affected BC production while optical density was poorly correlated with polymer production.
Airlift work showed oxygen-enriched gas increased BC production and altered final carbon mass balance.
Hypoxia-signaling engineering supports regulatory oxygen effects rather than a simple more-O2 rule.

safety_scope: Non-operational preregistration only. Any gas-transfer, pressure, or culture work must follow appropriate laboratory SOPs; no donor human milk, placenta, or human tissue is used.
